name: Ritchey-Chrétien telescope
definition: folded-path reflector with a hyperbolic concave primary and a hyperbolic convex secondary mirror and no full-aperture corrector.
reason: Own optical design (kind axis), a type-of-build filter at the shop; makers built only around it (RC Optical Systems, Officina Stellare).

name: Cassegrain reflector telescope
definition: folded-path reflector with a concave primary and a convex secondary mirror, no full-aperture corrector, other than the Ritchey-Chrétien; classical and Dall-Kirkham designs.
reason: Cassegrain is its own type-of-build filter beside Schmidt-Cassegrain and Newton on the fetched page; no tree kind is an all-mirror folded design.
A telescope optimised for imaging is built on one of the design kinds; photographic use is an attribute or tag (C10 retail facet, C2(b)).

name: Klevtsov-Cassegrain
reason: Cassegrain variant with a small sub-aperture corrector near the secondary: a design many makers could make, non-maker named form of the new Cassegrain kind.

name: Maksutov-Newtonian
reason: Side-focus Newtonian layout with a meniscus corrector; the Newtonian definition covers it; non-maker named form, as the Dobsonian (C-18).

name: Schmidt-Newtonian
reason: Side-focus Newtonian layout with a Schmidt corrector plate; the Newtonian definition covers it; non-maker named form.

name: Telescope tripod or pier
definition: tripod or pier made to carry a telescope mount head; a universal camera tripod is D4 (K-15).
reason: Sold apart in the shop's mount-accessory branch; made for telescope mount heads, so a C6 part (S3); universal tripods stay D4.

name: Mount counterweight
definition: weight made to slide on an equatorial mount's counterweight shaft to balance the telescope.
reason: Separate part type sold for telescope mounts (S3); no part kind covers it.

name: Telescope tube rings
definition: pair of rings or clamp that holds a telescope tube on a mount's dovetail or saddle.
reason: Separate part type in the mount-accessory branch; made only for telescopes (S3).

name: Polar scope
definition: small scope or camera fitted to an equatorial mount to align its axis on the celestial pole.
reason: Separate part type made for equatorial mounts (S3); neither mount kind nor eyepiece covers it.

name: Equatorial wedge
definition: tilted plate that sets an alt-azimuth fork mount at the observer's latitude so it tracks equatorially.
reason: Separate part type sold for telescope mounts (S3); not a mount itself.

name: Eye loupe
definition: loupe in a cup held in the eye socket by the brow, leaving both hands free; also called a watchmaker's loupe.
reason: Own subcategory at the shop; the lens is held a fifth way (eye socket), the leaf's kind axis; not handheld, folding, stand or head-worn.
Video magnifier made and sold as a low-vision aid: H2 by step 2 note (K-38); an inspection camera on a stand is a digital microscope.

name: Stand magnifier
reason: Lens on a desk clamp or arm stand is a stand magnifier (desk stand); illumination is an attribute (memo 4b).

name: Erlenmeyer flask
reason: Erlenmeyer, volumetric and round-bottom flask kinds exist (C6.3.1.02-04); Fernbach, shake and similar flasks are named forms of the nearest one.

name: Laboratory condenser
definition: glass tube with a cooling jacket or coil that turns vapour back into liquid in distillation or reflux.
reason: Cools a sample's vapour: the leaf's 'cool' action, not a vessel that holds or measures; no tree kind covers it.

name: Laboratory autoclave
definition: pressure chamber that sterilises instruments, media and waste with steam.
reason: Listed as its own equipment type on the fetched page; neither oven nor incubator sterilises under pressure.

name: Laboratory shaker
definition: platform that shakes or swirls vessels at a set speed to mix or aerate samples.
reason: Listed as its own equipment type; a device, so C6.3.2 (its leaf text should add 'mix').

name: Rotary evaporator
definition: apparatus that removes solvent from a sample by turning its flask in a warm bath under reduced pressure.
reason: Separates a sample (leaf action); its own equipment type on the harvester's page; no tree kind covers it.

name: Laminar-flow cabinet
definition: clean bench that blows filtered air over the work surface to keep samples free of contamination.
reason: Protects the sample, not the user: different airflow and use from the fume hood (C6.3.2.06); sold as its own type.

name: Biosafety cabinet
definition: filtered, ventilated cabinet that protects the user, the sample and the room during work with biological agents.
reason: Sold and compared apart from fume hoods and clean benches (filtration class); encloses biological work, a distinct device type.
Stabilisation is an attribute; filed by prism design C6.1.1.01 or C6.1.1.02 (memo 4b, precedence 1, CV-24).
Rangefinding is an attribute (K-148); Swarovski EL Range already sits under roof-prism binoculars C6.1.1.02.

name: Storm glass
definition: sealed glass vessel of a camphor solution whose crystals change with the weather, sold as a weather indicator.
reason: Sold in the weather-instrument category under its own generic name; no kind covers it; working, not a replica (precedence 10). Leaf provisional.
